{{Short description|Geometric structure used in certain particle interactions}}
[[File:Amplituhedron-0c.png|thumb|Notional amplituhedron visualization]]
In [[mathematics]] and [[theoretical physics]] (especially [[twistor string theory]]), an '''amplituhedron''' is a geometric structure introduced in 2013 by [[Nima Arkani-Hamed]] and Jaroslav Trnka. It enables simplified calculation of [[particle]] interactions in some [[quantum field]] theories. In [[Planar Yang–Mills theory|planar ''N'' = 4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory]], also equivalent to the perturbative [[Topological string theory#B-model|topological B model string theory]] in [[twistor space]], an amplituhedron is defined as a mathematical space known as the positive [[Grassmannian]].<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014">{{cite journal |last1=Arkani-Hamed |first1=Nima |last2=Trnka |first2=Jaroslav |year=2014 |title=The Amplituhedron |journal=[[Journal of High Energy Physics]] |volume=2014 |issue=10 |pages=30 |doi=10.1007/JHEP10(2014)030 |arxiv=1312.2007 |bibcode = 2014JHEP...10..030A |s2cid=7717260 }}</ref><ref name="Witten">{{cite journal|last=Witten|first=Edward|title=Perturbative Gauge Theory As A String Theory In Twistor Space|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|year=2004|volume=252|series=1|issue=1|pages=189–258|doi=10.1007/s00220-004-1187-3|arxiv=hep-th/0312171|bibcode = 2004CMaPh.252..189W |s2cid=14300396}}</ref>

Amplituhedron theory challenges the notion that [[spacetime]] [[principle of locality|locality]] and [[unitarity (physics)|unitarity]] are necessary components of a model of particle interactions. Instead, they are treated as properties that emerge from an underlying phenomenon.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Bourjaily Cachazo Goncharov 2012">{{cite arXiv|eprint=1212.5605|first1=Nima|last1=Arkani-Hamed|last2=Bourjaily|first2=Jacob L.|first3=Freddy|last3=Cachazo|last4=Goncharov|first4=Alexander B.|first5=Alexander|last5=Postnikov|first6=Jaroslav|last6=Trnka|title=Scattering Amplitudes and the Positive Grassmannian|class=hep-th|date=2012}}</ref><ref name=ohanlon20130919>{{cite web|url=https://psmag.com/environment/feel-space-time-maybe-exisitng-66647/|title=How to Feel About Space and Time Maybe Not Existing|publisher=Pacific Standard|author= Ryan O'Hanlon | date=September 19, 2013}}</ref>

The connection between the amplituhedron and scattering amplitudes is a conjecture that has passed many non-trivial checks, including an understanding of how locality and unitarity arise as consequences of positivity.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" /> Research has been led by [[Nima Arkani-Hamed]]. [[Edward Witten]] described the work as "very unexpected" and said that "it is difficult to guess what will happen or what the lessons will turn out to be".<ref name="Quandra20130917">{{cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/physicists-discover-geometry-underlying-particle-physics-20130917/|title=A Jewel at the Heart of Quantum Physics|author=Natalie Wolchover|author-link=Natalie Wolchover|work=[[Quanta Magazine]]|date=September 17, 2013}}</ref>

== Description ==
When [[subatomic particle]]s interact, different outcomes are possible. The evolution of the various possibilities is called a "tree", and the [[probability amplitude]] of a given outcome is called its [[scattering amplitude]]. According to the principle of [[unitarity (physics)|unitarity]], the sum of the probabilities (the squared moduli of the probability amplitudes) for every possible outcome is 1.

The [[On shell and off shell|on-shell]] scattering process "tree" may be described by a positive [[Grassmannian]], a structure in [[algebraic geometry]] analogous to a [[convex polytope]], that generalizes the idea of a [[simplex]] in [[projective space]].<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Bourjaily Cachazo Goncharov 2012" /> A [[polytope]] is the ''n''-dimensional analogue of a 3-dimensional [[polyhedron]], the values being calculated in this case are scattering amplitudes, and so the object is called an ''amplituhedron''.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" />

Using [[twistor theory]], Britto–Cachazo–Feng–Witten recursion ([[BCFW recursion]]) relations involved in the scattering process may be represented as a small number of twistor diagrams. These diagrams effectively provide the recipe for constructing the positive Grassmannian, i.e. the amplituhedron, which may be captured in a single equation.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Bourjaily Cachazo Goncharov 2012" /> The scattering amplitude can thus be thought of as the volume of a certain polytope, the positive Grassmannian, in momentum twistor space.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" />

When the volume of the amplituhedron is calculated in the [[1/N expansion|planar limit]] of [[N = 4 super Yang–Mills|''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;4 ''D''&nbsp;=&nbsp;4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory]], it describes the [[scattering amplitude]]s of particles described by this theory.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" />

The twistor-based representation provides a recipe for constructing specific cells in the Grassmannian which assemble to form a positive Grassmannian, i.e., the representation describes a specific [[cellular decomposition|cell decomposition]] of the positive Grassmannian.

The recursion relations can be resolved in many different ways, each giving rise to a different representation, with the final amplitude expressed as a sum of on-shell processes in different ways as well. Therefore, any given on-shell representation of scattering amplitudes is not unique, but all such representations of a given interaction yield the same amplituhedron.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" />

The twistor approach is relatively abstract. While amplituhedron theory provides an underlying geometric model, the geometrical space is not physical spacetime and is also best understood as abstract.<ref name="ananth2017">Anil Ananthaswamy; "The New Shape of Reality", ''New Scientist'', volume 235, issue 3136, 29 July 2017, pages 28–31. {{doi|10.1016/S0262-4079(17)31472-0}}.</ref>

==Implications==

The twistor approach simplifies calculations of particle interactions. In a conventional [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbative]] approach to quantum field theory, such interactions may require the calculation of thousands of [[Feynman diagrams]], most describing off-shell "virtual" particles which have no directly observable existence.  In contrast, [[twistor theory]] provides an approach in which scattering amplitudes can be computed in a way that yields much simpler expressions.<ref name=drum20130918>{{cite web|url=https://www.motherjones.com/kevin-drum/2013/09/space-time-illusion-amplituhedron|title=Maybe Space-Time Is Just an Illusion|author=Kevin Drum|publisher=Mother Jones|date=September 18, 2013}}</ref> Amplituhedron theory calculates scattering amplitudes without referring to such virtual particles. This undermines the case for even a transient, unobservable existence for such virtual particles.<ref name="ananth2017"/>

The geometric nature of the theory suggests in turn that the nature of the universe, in both classical [[Theory of relativity|relativistic]] [[spacetime]] and [[quantum mechanics]], may be described with [[geometry]].<ref name="ananth2017"/>

Calculations can be done without assuming the quantum mechanical properties of [[Principle of locality|locality]] and [[Unitarity (physics)|unitarity]]. In amplituhedron theory, locality and unitarity arise as a direct consequence of positivity.<ref name="ohanlon20130919" /> They are encoded in the positive geometry of the amplituhedron, via the singularity structure of the integrand for scattering amplitudes.<ref name="Arkani-Hamed Trnka 2014" /> Arkani-Hamed suggests this is why amplituhedron theory simplifies scattering-amplitude calculations: in the Feynman-diagrams approach, locality is manifest, whereas in the amplituhedron approach, it is implicit.<ref>{{cite book |last=Musser |first=George |year=2015 |title=Spooky Action at a Distance |url=https://archive.org/details/spookyactionatdi0000muss |url-access=registration |pages=[https://archive.org/details/spookyactionatdi0000muss/page/40 40–41] |publisher=Farrar, Straus and Giroux |location=New York |isbn=978-0-374-53661-9 }}</ref>
